layer_description: This layer contains the most general norms: scope clauses, core concepts, basic principles, and high-level policy orientations that define the reach and architecture of the regime. Provisions here do not yet regulate a concrete procedure; they set the framework conditions within which all later rules operate, including exclusions, preserved competences, and overarching governance standards.

This layer establishes the institutional and normative framework for implementation: delegations of power, organizational arrangements, internal responsibilities, and rules that channel how the regime is to be applied. These provisions are more specific than foundational norms, but still operate at a framework level rather than prescribing a single technical step or deadline.

This layer translates the framework into concrete operative rules for defined procedures, categories of contracts, and specific legal effects. Provisions here regulate how a mechanism works in practice, including conditions, thresholds, allocation rules, admissibility criteria, and procedural sequences, but they still retain some generality and are not yet purely mechanical.

This layer contains the most detailed and execution-oriented provisions: publication duties, notice content, deadlines, calculation methods, evidentiary requirements, communication channels, and other micro-rules. It also includes targeted amendments, textual substitutions, commencement and repeal clauses, and transitional or saving provisions that manage legal continuity and the entry into force of changes.
